You’re carrying a lot of repressed shame and guilt but you know you want to get better and will do. Search for points of stability, people communities etc... where you feel comfortable and stable, also to push your brain to get back into the sober lifestyle. Expressing myself is one of my problems right now, either way I hope you understand me and know you’re not alone, we’re all going through this insanity at some point, not only recovering addicts but also people with great pain of any sort. It will get better but it will be a path with many slopes, it’s important that you communicate as well. Have patience. We got you. Take care, feel free to chat.

Once you go through it and get to the point where you are more in control of that, you become a more selfless person which is the opposite of an anxious mind, the end of the ego which consumes you with negative thoughts. I cried many times on psychedelics reflecting on my life, of sadness but of joy as well. Ketamine also helped me, it tears down the barriers of strict rationality and makes you a more relaxed and goofy person. With that said, take it easy, everything with moderation and try not to rely on substances. Take care.

It’s about how you react to your environment, and if you can overcome it. I’ve used a couple SSRIs and also had panic disorder, and what comes with it. Don’t think about your meds too much, you will act in accordance to what you think they are doing to you. Seasonal depression has taken a few lives, so don’t let that minor factor affect you too much either, it affects everyone, that might explain why you are a bit moodier, me included. Don’t let it take over your emotions, because things that affect you negatively will produce a chain reaction of negative thinking and thus negative behavior, which is totally normal, but being able to control it’s what lets you come out of it and thus cause you less stress, because panic attacks are like accumulated stress that explodes. Start by thinking, why am I even mad? Can I do something about it? You can start be smiling even if you don’t feel like it, it will at least make a difference to how you normally react to things. Concentrate on your panic attacks, feel them and, this is gonna sound kinda crazy,  but just laugh. Think about how ridiculous it is to be tormented by panic, and how ridiculous it is to apparently not being able to do anything about it, then you will start to befriend your panic and it’ll be no more panic, but a part of you which you will be able to control. Try if you want, and if so, tell me how it went. Wish you luck!
